The authors demonstrated RCS reduction of 20 to 25 dB using a prototype system.
The frequency range over which the RCS reduction was observed was 4 to 14 GHz.

The theoretical model developed for the plasma cloaking process includes scattering contributions from the plasma-vacuum interface, partial reflections from the plasma, and collisional absorption in the plasma.
The plasma frequency is the frequency at which the plasma becomes overdense and electromagnetic waves are totally reflected.
The Debye length is the distance over which the plasma density changes significantly.
The condition for the electron temperature to be very small is that the mean free path between collisions must be much smaller than the Debye length.
The expression for the dielectric constant of a collisionless plasma is ε = 1 - (ωp^2 / ω^2).
The propagation constant for an electromagnetic wave in a collisional plasma is k = k0 - iα.
The collision frequency determines the rate at which electrons collide with the background gas molecules.
The expression for the attenuation of an electromagnetic wave in a uniform plasma is α = (ωp^2 / (ω^2 + ν^2)).
The maximum attenuation observed in the plasma-filled waveguide was 61 dB.
The frequency range over which the maximum attenuation was observed was 4-6 GHz.
The scaling of the attenuation with the collision frequency is α ∝ ν^2.
The authors used a seed-gas/UV photoionization technique to produce the plasma.
The plasma was produced in a sealed ceramic enclosure with a microwave reflector and a plasma generator inside it.
The RCS reduction was measured using a compact radar range at Hughes Aircraft's Microwave Products Division in Torrance.
